name: Tawang Monastery (Gaden Namgyal Lhatse)
description: Largest Buddhist monastery in India and one of the largest in Asia, founded in 1680-81 by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso under the guidance of the 5th Dalai Lama. Perched at about 3,000 m overlooking the Tawang Chu valley, it belongs to the Gelug school and houses an 8 m gilded Buddha statue, ancient scriptures, and around 450 monks.
facts: Founded 1680-1681 by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso
Elevation about 3,000 m (10,000 ft)
Largest monastery in India; houses ~450 monks
Birthplace region of the 6th Dalai Lama nearby
Open daily; museum entry low fee
Inner Line Permit required for the district

name: Sangetsar Tso (Madhuri Lake / Shonga-tser Lake)
description: High-altitude lake at about 3,708 m on the road toward Bum La Pass, formed by an earthquake that submerged a forest, leaving dead tree trunks standing in the water. Popularly known as Madhuri Lake after a Bollywood film shoot; surrounded by rugged Himalayan peaks.
facts: Elevation ~3,708 m (12,165 ft)
About 35 km north of Tawang town
Created by earthquake; submerged forest trunks visible
Also called Shonga-tser or Sangestar Tso
Special Army permit often needed beyond basic ILP
Best Apr-Oct; road can be rough

name: Sela Pass (Se La)
description: High-altitude mountain pass at 4,170 m on the border of Tawang and West Kameng districts, carrying NH-13 and the main road access to Tawang. Often snow-covered; features prayer-flag-adorned gates, nearby Sela Lake, and now bypassed in part by the Sela Tunnel for all-weather connectivity.
facts: Elevation 4,170 m (13,700 ft)
On border of Tawang and West Kameng districts
About 78 km from Tawang town
Sela Tunnel opened for all-weather access
Named after local Monpa woman Sela; Jaswant Garh nearby
Snow possible year-round; check road conditions

name: Nuranang Falls (Jang Falls / Bong Bong Falls)
description: Spectacular ~100 m high curtain waterfall near Jang town on the Tawang–Bomdila route, fed by the Nuranang Chu originating from Sela Pass slopes. Popular stop with a small hydel plant at the base; featured in Bollywood films.
facts: Height about 100 m (330 ft)
2 km from Jang town; ~40 km from Tawang
Also known as Jung or Bong Bong Falls
Nuranang Chu joins Tawang River below
Named in local lore after Monpa girl Nura
Accessible by road; best monsoon to post-monsoon for volume

name: Urgelling Monastery (Ugyenling Gompa)
description: Historic small monastery founded around 1489, recognized as the birthplace of the 6th Dalai Lama Tsangyang Gyatso (born 1683). Quiet Nyingma-school gompa a few kilometres from Tawang town, offering a more intimate spiritual experience than the larger Tawang Monastery.
facts: Birthplace of 6th Dalai Lama Tsangyang Gyatso (1683)
Founded ~1489 by Urgen Sangpo
About 3–5 km from Tawang town
Smaller and quieter than Tawang Monastery
Sacred trees and historical inscriptions
Free entry; combine with Tawang Monastery visit

name: Tawang War Memorial
description: Memorial in the form of a Buddhist chorten/stupa dedicated to Indian soldiers who lost their lives in the 1962 Sino-Indian War. Located on a hill overlooking Tawang town; names of fallen inscribed on granite, with prayer flags and a solemn atmosphere.
facts: Honours soldiers of the 1962 Indo-China War
Chorten/stupa architecture ~12 m high
Names engraved on black granite
Overlooking Tawang town and valleys
Free entry; respectful visit recommended
Near town centre; easy access

name: Bum La Pass
description: High-altitude border pass at about 4,600 m on the India–China Line of Actual Control, historically a trade route and site of fierce fighting in 1962. Features a Border Personnel Meeting point and stone cairn symbolising relations; restricted access requiring special permits.
facts: Elevation ~4,600 m (15,200 ft)
About 37 km from Tawang town
Border Personnel Meeting point with China
Historical 1962 war site and old trade route
Special Army/ILP permits required; SUVs recommended
Not always open to civilians; check status

name: Tawang Town
description: District headquarters and main tourist base in the high-altitude Monpa Buddhist heartland of western Arunachal Pradesh. Gateway for the monastery, lakes, passes and border areas; served by road via Sela Pass/Tunnel from the Assam plains.
facts: HQ of Tawang district; elevation ~2,700–3,000 m
Main base for Tawang Monastery and nearby sites
Inner Line Permit mandatory for Indian tourists
Road access via NH-13 / Sela Tunnel from Tezpur/Guwahati
Monpa culture, local handicrafts and markets
Nearest major air/rail links in Assam
